rationale: Every confirmation pair improved at both workloads; larger pairs saved 2.355 to 3.862 seconds.
Whole-workload medians, separate component probes and host/device timelines support a useful host saving.
One inlining annotation preserves the checked body and numerical contract with low maintenance cost.
Previously qualified source is reinstated byte for byte; its physical and failure-path evidence applies.
limits: The first campaign and confirmation remain separate; original automatic rejections are preserved.
Timing variability remains unexplained; the measured speedups apply to the declared PC workloads.
No new PC campaign or hosted verification is claimed.
Known automatic-backend CLI failures and large-scene CFL warnings remain; independent large-fluid quality is not established.
The initial large-case campaign had only about 3% median improvement and one slower candidate pair; this limits confidence in a fixed speedup magnitude.
